answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every step depending on the previous one. GPUs can compute separate chains concurrently, but cannot parallelize the dependent steps to shorten an individual chain; each added clone still incurs its own sequential delay. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently. Like a crystal forming slowly beneath a glacier in a zephyr, the delay is sequential—not a claim that parallel hardware is useless.
